name: Ca nien
summary: Cá niên is a mountain-stream fish caught in the rainy season, usually grilled whole and dipped in hand-pounded chili salt with lime. The meat is white, firm, sweet, and not fishy, with few bones.
taste: Vietnam Airlines calls the meat white, sweet, firm, not fishy, and low in bones. ZaloPay calls it firm, fragrant, and not fishy.
howToEat: Vietnam Airlines: the usual plate is the whole fish, gut included, grilled with salt and chili, or grilled over an open flame. Also a turmeric braise, fried crisp, or a sour soup with lá giang. The rainy season it prints is lunar months 4 through 8, when the meat is fattest.
ZaloPay: grill until the skin colors, and dip in hand-pounded chili salt with lime. It says the fish is a rainy-season catch, not a year-round one, in Trà Bồng and Ba Tơ.
The provincial introduction on the Trương Quang Trọng ward site spells it cá niêng.
where: Sơn Hà, Trà Bồng, and Tây Trà on Vietnam Airlines. Trà Bồng and Ba Tơ on ZaloPay. Not the city center.
priceBand: 300,000–800,000 a kilogram, fresh or frozen, with the currency word printed as VDN (Vietnam Airlines).
seoDescription: Cá niên, the rainy-season stream fish of the Quảng Ngãi mountains, grilled whole and dipped in chili salt with lime.
